deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics on it. It is a meteorological observation log in tabular form, headed '1827'. Each row is one day, from Nov. 3 to Nov. 13, 1827, and each day is marked with its planetary weekday symbol: ♄ Saturday, ☉ Sunday, ☾ Monday, ♂ Tuesday, ☿ Wednesday, ♃ Thursday, ♀ Friday.

The columns are reading times: 9h Vormittag (9 a.m.), then 0h (noon), 3h, 6h, 9h and 12h (midnight). At each time two numbers are given:
(a) A barometer height, evidently in millimetres. The values lie between 735.40 and 755.05, which fits a station at roughly 150 m altitude such as Göttingen.
(b) A small number between 3.9 and 7.9. This is a temperature, almost certainly degrees Réaumur, the usual scale at the time. It is most likely the attached thermometer used for the temperature correction of the barometer, though it could be the outside air temperature (unsure).

The series shows a deep pressure minimum:
- Pressure falls from about 753–755 on Nov. 4–5.
- It reaches 735.40 at midnight Nov. 9/10.
- It recovers to 746.5 by midnight Nov. 10.
- It dips again to about 739 on Nov. 11.
- It returns to about 753.7 on Nov. 13.

The log stops at 3h on Nov. 13. The 9h reading of Nov. 11 is incomplete (739.?, with no temperature). Several entries are overwritten corrections.

Nothing is computed. There are no means or reductions to 0°, and no derivation. The page is raw data. It probably relates to Gauss's interest in barometric heights and meteorology, which ran parallel to his geodetic survey work; the surrounding pages are triangulation direction corrections (Bentheim, Ulsen, Kirchhesepe, Coeverden) and a Gauss-sum computation.

The weekday labels are internally consistent: 1 Jan 1827 was a Monday, and 3 Nov 1827 is 306 days later. 306 ≡ 5 mod 7, so 3 Nov falls on a Saturday, matching ♄.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible since there is no computation.
The 9h entry on Nov. 11 is incomplete (decimals illegible or missing, and no temperature).
Several readings are overwritten corrections in the manuscript itself: Nov. 7 9h Vorm 748.46, Nov. 8 0h 744.64 (and its temperature 5.4), Nov. 9 9h 736.99, and Nov. 10 6h 743.91 / 5.8.

results.what: Hourly barometer and thermometer readings, Nov. 3–13, 1827, at six fixed times per day
results.usually_credited_to: Routine practice of many observers (e.g., Göttingen observatory records)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a raw weather and barometer log with no mathematical content. Gauss is well known to have kept such meteorological and barometric records.

checkable.asserts: 3 Nov 1827 is 306 days after Monday 1 Jan 1827, so it falls 5 weekdays later, i.e. on a Saturday, consistent with the ♄ label.
The total pressure range in the table is 755.05 - 735.40 = 19.65 mm.
The pressure fell 7.13 mm between noon and midnight on Nov. 9.
The pressure rose 11.11 mm from midnight Nov. 9 to midnight Nov. 10.

transcription_corrections: The column header is probably '9^h Vorm.' (9 a.m.) rather than '9^u Vorm'. A stray 'Nov. 3' in the header cell is crossed out.
Nov. 4, 12h: the temperature reads 6,1; the final digit is partly obscured but 6.1 is likely.
Nov. 11, 9h: the barometer value is '739.?' with the decimals illegible, and a dash stands in place of the temperature.
Nov. 8, 0h: '744.64' is written over another value (possibly 744.84), and its temperature 5.4 is also overwritten.
The next page is numbered 214, not 314 (folio sequence 212, 213, 214).
The marginal numbers at the left edge (+2.62482, -2.778, 9.00820, 9.121, ES 1″315, etc.) are not part of this page. They belong to the facing previous folio (212) and show through in the photograph.
